items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. Asimismo, incorpora procedimientos para auditoría me

items.summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.

items.summary: Language functions not only as a means of transmitting information but also as a repository of cultural knowledge, collective experience, and culturally shaped patterns of thought. Consequently, translation involves more than the transfer of lexical and grammatical information between languages. It also requires the interpretation and reconstruction of meanings that are embedded within particular cultural contexts. This issue becomes especially evident in the translation of idioms, proverbs, metaphors, realia, and other culture-specific expressions whose meanings cannot always be derived from their individual lexical components. In Translation Studies, such elements are commonly discussed as culture-specific items (CSIs), which may require particular strategies to preserve their semantic, pragmatic, and cultural dimensions in the target language (Aixelá, 1996).
tags: Idiomatic expressions provide a particularly clear illustration of the relationship between language and culture.

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). items.summary: Abstract We present a comprehensive, universal, abstract group-theoretic, module-theoretic, and category-theoretic formalization of bijectively separated rank arithmetic . Given an arbitrary family of algebraic groups {Gi}r i=1 and elements Pi ∈ Gi with finite multiplicative orders oi = ord(Pi), we establish that the additive rank-coordinate space A(P) = Qri=1 Z/oiZ is canonically isomorphic to the external direct product of cyclic power orbits G(P) = Qri=1⟨Pi⟩ under the coordinate evaluation map ΦP(([ni]oi)i) = (Pnii)i. We prove that coordinatewise multiplication in the multiplicative state space corresponds strictly to coordinatewise addition of discrete expo- nent rank classes without introducing analytic logarithms, continuous curves, branch cuts, or topological ambiguities. We extend this framework to general category- theoretic limits, establishing that sub-space coordinate projections and factor permutation reindexings form natural transformations in the category of groups Grp. Furthermore, when lane outputs collapse into a single target background group H, we isolate the exact relation subgroup KP =ker(ΨP) and prove the quotient isomorphism A(P)/KP∼= ⟨P1, . . . , Pr⟩ ≤ H, measuring the precise algebraic information lost during scalar collapse. Finally, we formulate the extension to infinite complex power orbits , polynomial root reconstruction via Newton symmetrization of ranked power arrays Pr ∈ Cr×r, Chinese Remainder Theorem grid decompositions over composite moduli, native linear rank complexity bounds Θ(m), and an axiomatic minimal proof assistant kernel . Keywords: Abstract algebra, cyclic groups, direct products, exponent coordinates, re- lation lattices, projection functors, natural transformations, Newton identities, Chinese Remainder Theorem, rank complexity. items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code supporting an assembly-first workflow with raw-read reconstruction for publicly available sequencing records. Starting from 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,687 records had no analyzable public genome input, leaving 42,591 records with an analyzable genome input. Of these, two were excluded during final cohort harmonization, resulting in a final analytical collection of 42,589 K. pneumoniae genomes. This collection comprised 40,093 genomes represented by usable public assemblies and 2,496 genomes reconstructed from publicly available sequencing reads. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Sequence data should be retrieved from the relevant public repositories using the accession identifiers provided in the manifests. The archived materials support reproduction of the post-assembly cohort audit, statistical summaries, and figures. The exact raw-read preprocessing commands used for the rescued genomes were not retained; consequently, adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are not represented as reproducible components of this deposit. Reconstructed and deposited assemblies were nevertheless evaluated using the same post-assembly quality-control criteria before inclusion in the final analytical collection. items.summary: This poster presents a lunar surface simulation framework and synthetic dataset for evaluating visual-domain zero-shot sim-to-real transfer in lunar perception. The framework integrates terrain reconstruction, lunar surface appearance modelling, realistic illumination, and synthetic data generation to support controlled evaluation of visual fidelity and cross-dataset segmentation performance. Experimental results show that the proposed dataset achieves lower feature-space distance to real lunar imagery and stronger zero-shot segmentation performance across multiple model architectures. The work further investigates mixed-training strategies and key simulation design factors. Presented at the Towards Sustainability and Resiliency of Field Robotics Workshop, IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2025), Hangzhou, China, 20 October 2025. Honourable Mention for Best Poster Award.
items.title: A Novel Lunar Surface Simulation Framework Enabling Visual Domain Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer

items.summary: Data accompanying N. Vauquier, B. M. L. Srivastava, S. A. Hosseini and E. Vincent, "Legally validated evaluation framework for voice anonymization", Interspeech 2025, pages 3229 to 3233, doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1699. The paper introduces two metrics, Singling Out and Linkability, that translate the singling out and linkability criteria of the Article 29 Working Party's Opinion 05/2014 on Anonymization Techniques into quantities that can be measured on speech. The framework was formally validated by the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL). This record holds the data needed to reproduce the paper's results. The reference implementation is at https://github.com/brijmohan/voice-anonymization-legal-eval CONTENTS Dataset definitions, unchanged from version 1.0.0: cv11-A-filelist (19.5 MB): the Mozilla Common Voice 11.0 clips forming subset A, 22,024 speakers with at least 2 minutes of speech each. cv11-B-filelist (83.3 MB): the clips forming subset B, 4,949 speakers with at least 3 minutes each. Subset B's speakers are a subset of A's, with disjoint utterances. Cosine score matrices, new in version 2.0.0, 12 files totalling 5.2 GB: scores_<attacker>_L<length>.npy: a 22,024 x 4,949 float32 array per attacker model and conversation length. Entry [i, j] is the cosine similarity between enrollment speaker i of subset A and test speaker j of subset B. scores_<attacker>_L<length>.npy.json: a sidecar per matrix giving the row and column speaker order, so each matrix is self describing. MANIFEST.json: SHA-256 checksums and shapes for every file. The four attacker models differ in what their speaker embedding extractor was trained on: original : original speech, evaluated on original speech. ignorant : original speech. semi_informed : speech anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2022 baseline B1.a. informed : speech anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2024 baseline B1. Conversation length L is the number of utterances averaged per speaker, and takes the values 1, 3 and 30. Test data for the three attackers is anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2024 baseline B1. USING THE MATRICES pip install git+https://github.com/brijmohan/voice-anonymization-legal-eval from legal_eval.io import load_score_matrix from legal_eval.sweeps import linkability_sweep m = load_score_matrix("scores_informed_L1.npy") print(linkability_sweep(m, speaker_counts=[20, 100, 1000, 10000]).mean()) To check a download against the published results: python examples/03_verify_against_score_matrices.py --release-dir . That recomputes all 2,640 published Linkability points. Expect a worst case difference of about 0.005, which is Monte Carlo noise from averaging five runs. WHAT THE MATRICES CONTAIN These are similarity scores rather than speaker embeddings, but the distinction is smaller than it sounds and it is worth being explicit. Each matrix is the product of two sets of unit norm x-vectors, so its rank is bounded by the embedding dimension rather than by its shape. Measured on a random 3,000 x 3,000 block, the singular value spectrum collapses by four orders of magnitude immediately after index 256, which is the x-vector dimension, and a rank 256 reconstruction reproduces the released scores to within 2e-07. A recipient can therefore recover similarity structure that was never released, link a speaker across the four released conditions, and cluster speakers by voice similarity. ON THE SPEAKER LABELS Row and column labels are internal pseudonyms of the form spk-f-20851, not Mozilla Common Voice client identifiers. They should not be relied on as a safeguard. The subset file lists in this record are public, Common Voice publishes a client identifier for every clip, and the evaluation pipeline is openly reproducible, so a determined party could recompute an original condition matrix and align it to the released one to recover the mapping. items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.
items.title: Scientific supplement for Evidence Access and Adverse Product Content in AI Assessment

items.summary: Reproducing a machine-learning result requires knowing how the experiment was run: the data, the model and its size, the optimiser, the learning rate, the batch size, the number of steps, the hardware and the seeds. This information is scattered through a paper---often only in a table caption or an appendix---and is increasingly extracted automatically by language-model pipelines, whose evaluations report how often they are right. We ask the two questions those evaluations leave open: when a pipeline is wrong, does it know it is wrong; and how much human effort does it take to find out? We build a benchmark of 80 arXiv machine-learning papers and annotate 24 of them (240 field decisions), 12 of them through two independent annotation passes, carrying verbatim, line-numbered evidence for every reported and every absent field; the passes agree on 97.5% of presence/absence decisions (Cohen's κ = 0.94), and the residual disagreements are adjudicated under a written scope rule. On that gold standard we run six extraction conditions of increasing agency---a single untruncated prompt, a tool-using agent, schema constraints, table/appendix re-reading, per-field self-assessment with a suspect flag, and mandatory evidence back-linking---over three difficulty strata, 432 full-paper extractions in total. Four results. First, agency buys no accuracy: present recall varies by one percentage point across all six conditions (0.883–0.894) while wall-clock time varies threefold. Second, honesty is a different quantity: 92% of the 387 wrong values were returned without any indication of doubt, and the share of returned values that are silently wrong falls from 12.7% to 5.5% only in the condition asked to flag its own doubts; requiring an evidence quote for every value restores the silent rate to 11.2% because it crowds out the doubt flag. Third, the errors are not inventions: every returned value that carries a checkable anchor occurs somewhere in the paper, and 375 of the 387 errors are values the document does contain—misattributions that belong to another configuration, another table, or the reference list, or values lifted from elsewhere in the paper—which is why a gold-standard-free anchor audit detects none of them (we report that as a negative result, with the five PDF text-layer artefacts it originally fired on pinned as a 22-case regression test). Fourth, human verification is the binding cost and it is predictable: verifying one field by hand requires a median of 12 candidate passages (up to 273; 4,707 in total for the gold sample) against one passage with an evidence link, although 4 of 25 spot-checked links failed adjudication, three of them because the quoted line does not hold the value. All corpus, prompts, gold annotations, adjudication records, raw runs, per-item API costs and analysis scripts are released with the paper, together with a per-session cost ledger ( runs/session-costs.json : the grid itself cost $2.84, the 644 sessions recorded in the released artefacts cost $3.22).

items.summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). items.summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. Code: MIT licence. Data files: CC BY 4.0.

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

The package includes the source tables for every main and supplementary figure and table, model-score summaries, fine-mapping benchmark tables, AUROC resampling summaries, the matched FILER functional-annotation enrichment analysis (inputs, results, and QC), the follow-up analyses that dissect the group difference (score anatomy, resampling, LD, allele frequency, label transfer, within-gene evaluation, annotation baselines), the model-first LD-reduced evaluation (configuration, results, and QC), the eQTLGen replication summary, and row-level prediction tables. The package is split into several archives; the top-level README and MANIFEST describe every file and how the archives fit together. No individual-level genotypes or sample identifiers are included. Analysis code for model scoring, summary analyses, and manuscript figure and table generation is available at https://github.com/Xinyu-Sun/s2f_snp_eqtl_analysis_code, commit b5a9e1270f431a82265d63f0b90ee17eabb9da6c. Version 2026-10-03.

items.summary: Reviewer reproducibility materials for the manuscript Historical Window Choice and Forecast Horizon in Road Traffic Forecasting: Evidence from Great Britain, 1976–2025. This package contains the frozen analytical data, preserved source code, protocol and audit documents, archived numerical outputs, reviewer-facing reproduction scripts, validation files, and checksums used to support the reported analyses. The package also includes documented post-hoc sensitivity analyses, uncertainty reporting, simulation checks, provenance records, and reproducibility validations. Historical protocol and addendum files are retained in their original form to preserve the chronological audit trail. This version aligns the repository metadata with the final manuscript title and incorporates the manuscript’s latest transparency and reporting updates, including the fixed-target 2017–2025 interval-coverage table derived from previously archived target-level outputs. items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. items.summary: Companion archive for the article Accuracy is not reliability: abstention-aware evaluation of large language models on bio-bibliographic claim verification in classical Islamic scholarship (Information Processing & Management, Elsevier, 2026, in press). Contents: the ISNAD benchmark (1,986 scored Turkish claims across five probe types) and the 360-item Turkish/Arabic GAL replication set with gold labels; freeze and exclusion manifests; 64,216 raw model-output records; blank expert-study forms with answer keys; and six analysis scripts with fixed seeds that regenerate the article's tables. Item-level expert responses are not released, at the annotator's request. Licences: code (analysis/) MIT; data (data/, human_studies/) CC BY 4.0. Factual information drawn from the TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi and from Brockelmann's History of the Arabic Written Tradition; no rights are claimed over those works.

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set].
